terms.comment: The classical verb for rubbing writing off a wax tablet, and Traupman’s for deleting on a computer: the sense has not moved.
Classically to strike a name off a list by pricking dots against it (Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens cites a scholar of 1698 who struck out false entries from a dictionary.

evidence: Tac. A. 4.42 (Lewis & Short): aliquem albō ērādere
terms.comment: Scraping writing off a tablet or a list; Lewis & Short: ante-classical and from Augustus on.

evidence: Cic. Arch. 9: ūnīus nōminis litūra (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The smoothed wax where something written has been rubbed out.

phrases.latin: esse putā cērās, licet haec membrāna vocētur: dēlēbis, quotiēns scrīpta novāre volēs
phrases.english: think of it as wax, though it is called parchment: you will rub it out whenever you want to write afresh

sources: Lewis & Short: deleo · Lewis & Short: expungo
Lewis & Short: erado
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 260, 302, 29.
